sections.heading: A blog engine that is also your whole website
sections.subheading: Write in Markdown or in the browser. open.blog builds a fast static site with pages, recipes, lessons, services, documentation and a front page you arrange yourself. No database, and no tracking of your readers.

image.alt: Studio, the browser editor, open on a recipe: fields for servings and times above the recipe's words, with Update and See how it looks at the bottom.

sections.markdown:
## Everything here is a working example

This site is built with open.blog, from the same files you would write. Each part of it shows one thing the engine does, with the source beside it.

- **Write.** Call-outs, footnotes, buttons, maps, before-and-after photos, diagrams and quizzes. [The writer's toolkit](/series/writers-toolkit/)
- **Cook.** Recipes that scale, time themselves and print. [From the kitchen](/series/from-the-kitchen/)
- **Teach.** Code readers run, edit and check in the page. [Teaching with code](/series/teaching-with-code/)
- **Sell your work.** Services, finished jobs, reviews and a quote form. [For trades and local businesses](/series/for-trades-and-local-business/)
- **Document.** A handbook with a sidebar and its own search. [Example handbook](/docs/)
- **Run it.** View counts, comments, feeds, search and your own look. [Running your blog](/series/running-your-blog/)

[The full tour](/features/) lists every feature with its example and its page in the documentation.

## More than a list of posts

A site needs pages that are not posts. open.blog has them, and each is a Markdown file or a card you arrange:

- **This front page** is sections in a file: a welcome, buttons, text, pictures, questions and lists. [How it is built](/sites/#the-front-page)
- **Pages** such as [About](/about/), [Questions](/faq/) and [Get started](/get-started/) live at their own addresses.
- **Collections** gather posts into [series](/series/), [recipes](/recipes/) and [services](/services/), each with its own page and, if you like, its own look.
- **A documentation section** sits [beside the blog](/docs/), or is the whole site.

[Kinds of sites you can build](/sites/) walks through each.

sections.markdown:
## Studio: the editor for people who do not want the files

Run `openblog serve --admin` and open `/admin`. Studio writes the same Markdown files, so nothing is locked in, and it works on a phone.

- Write, schedule and publish, with the page shown as readers will see it.
- Arrange the front page, change the look, and put up a different look for a season.
- See how many readers came and where from, and read their comments before they appear.

[Take the tour of Studio](/studio/)

items.question: Do I need a database or a server?
items.answer: No. The site is plain files, and any static host can serve it. Studio is a small program you run when you want to edit in the browser. [Deploying](https://journey-to-code-org.github.io/open.blog/docs/deploy/) lists the hosts.

items.question: Do I have to write Markdown?
items.answer: No. Studio has a visual editor and an **Add something** menu for buttons, pictures, maps and the rest. The files it writes are Markdown, so you can open them in any editor later. [Studio](/studio/)

items.question: Are my readers tracked?
items.answer: No. View counts, comments and share links are built in, with no cookies and no third-party scripts. [Views, comments and sharing](/posts/views-comments-and-sharing/)

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: Nothing. open.blog is free software under the GPL, version 3 or later. [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/journey-to-code-org/open.blog)
